lessons.title: How this learning lab works
outcomes: This site is a free learning lab about AI omni-channel agents.

lessons.title: Programs, files, and a notebook
outcomes: A program is a file the computer can run again.

lessons.title: Python values and functions
outcomes: A function takes an input and returns an output.

lessons.title: HTTP and JSON
outcomes: HTTP is a request and a response.

lessons.title: Secrets stay out of the file
outcomes: A key in a source file will be copied.

lessons.title: Tests and a small eval
outcomes: A test names an input and an expected output.

lessons.title: Transcription of a recording
outcomes: Wikipedia defines speech analytics as analyzing recorded calls to gather customer information.

lessons.title: Sentiment is a label
outcomes: Wikipedia defines sentiment analysis as identifying affective states and subjective information.

lessons.title: A QA score needs a rubric
outcomes: Wikipedia's speech-analytics page says the technology can point to where an agent may need coaching and can monitor service on calls.

lessons.title: Redaction
outcomes: Wikipedia's personal-data page says personally identifiable information is information related to an identifiable person, and that legal definitions differ by place.

lessons.title: Pitfalls
outcomes: A fluent transcript can still have the wrong word. Check it against audio you are allowed to hear.

lessons.title: Handoff to a person
outcomes: A handoff in this lab means a person continues the turn.

lessons.title: Guardrails
outcomes: OWASP's Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications is the community list this lab uses for model risks. It is not a contact-center certificate.

lessons.title: Consent and recording, as education
outcomes: This room is educational. It is not legal advice. The rule depends on the place, the parties, and the current text.

lessons.title: Evaluation and testing
outcomes: Keep a fixed set of lines you are allowed to use: a script you wrote, not a customer tape.

lessons.title: What this chapter will not claim
outcomes: No legal conclusion, and no sentence of the form 'you may record in this state.'

lessons.title: Words for this ecosystem
outcomes: Wikipedia defines speech analytics as analysis of recorded calls.

lessons.title: A mind map
outcomes: Put the person in the center. The channels around them are voice, chat, and message.

lessons.title: Sister technologies
outcomes: Workforce management, from Wikipedia, includes forecasting, scheduling, and time and attendance among its core processes. It is not the voice model.

lessons.title: An integration map
outcomes: Draw the live path: person, transport, voice session, tool, CRM note.

lessons.title: Bridges across platforms
outcomes: LiveKit's cascaded pipeline and Pipecat's processor list are two open descriptions of speech-to-text, a model, and text-to-speech.

lessons.title: Future hooks
outcomes: Pin the model id, the voice name, and the date you read the doc.

lessons.title: Tokens, not words
outcomes: A model reads tokens, which may be parts of words.

lessons.title: Next-token prediction
outcomes: The model assigns scores to possible next tokens.

lessons.title: Context windows
outcomes: The context window is how much text the call can see at once.

lessons.title: Sampling
outcomes: Temperature and related controls change how peaked the next-token choice is.

lessons.title: Hallucination
outcomes: A hallucination here means a confident claim the sources do not support.

lessons.title: Model cards and ids
outcomes: A model id is a name you pin, because names move.

lessons.title: A job, a shape, and a test
outcomes: A wish is not a job. Name the reader and the done check.

lessons.title: Messages
outcomes: Hosted APIs usually separate system, user, and tool messages. Confirm the current API.

lessons.title: Schemas
outcomes: A schema names the fields you will accept.

lessons.title: A golden set
outcomes: Ten to fifty checks beat one demo.

lessons.title: Latency and a toy budget
outcomes: Latency is time, usually milliseconds.

lessons.title: Prompt diff
outcomes: A diff shows the lines you changed.

lessons.title: Why retrieve
outcomes: A model does not contain your private notes.

lessons.title: Chunks
outcomes: A chunk is a piece you store and retrieve.

lessons.title: Embeddings
outcomes: An embedding is a list of numbers that stands for a text.

lessons.title: Retrieve, then read
outcomes: Search returns candidates. Reading decides.

lessons.title: Cite or refuse
outcomes: Every factual sentence needs a passage or a refusal.

lessons.title: Failure modes
outcomes: Missed retrieval: the passage exists and was not returned.

lessons.title: An agent is a loop
outcomes: An agent here means the model can choose a tool, see the result, and continue.

lessons.title: Tools and schemas
outcomes: A tool is a function with a name, a schema, and a side effect you understand.

lessons.title: Step caps and traces
outcomes: A step cap is the maximum number of tool rounds.

lessons.title: Human approval
outcomes: Some actions are hard to undo: sending, deleting, paying, changing a record.

lessons.title: ReAct, at learning depth
outcomes: ReAct interleaves a written reason and an action.

lessons.title: When not to use an agent
outcomes: Do not use a loop for a form with known fields.

lessons.title: The problem MCP names
outcomes: Tools written for one app are hard to reuse in another.

lessons.title: Host, client, and server
outcomes: The host is the application the person uses.

lessons.title: Tools, resources, and prompts
outcomes: A tool does something and returns a result.

lessons.title: Transports
outcomes: A transport carries the protocol messages.

lessons.title: Consent and roots
outcomes: The person should see which server and which tool are about to run.

lessons.title: A notes server on paper
outcomes: The server offers two resources: list notes, read note.

lessons.title: Omni-channel, for a learner
outcomes: Omni-channel here means one assistant pattern that can meet a person on more than one channel.

lessons.title: The voice loop
outcomes: A voice turn is: hear, understand, decide, speak.

lessons.title: A latency budget you label as a lesson
outcomes: People notice waits in voice more than in chat.

lessons.title: Chat and messaging beside voice
outcomes: Chat can show the quote on screen. Voice has to say it.

lessons.title: Handoff to a person
outcomes: Handoff means a person continues the turn.

lessons.title: What this lab will not claim
outcomes: No professional GenAI employment is claimed.

lessons.title: One GPU, then a cluster
outcomes: A GPU is a processor often used for the matrix math in model training and serving.

lessons.title: Colossus as a public story
outcomes: Colossus is the public name xAI has used for a large NVIDIA GPU cluster.

lessons.title: Cloud endpoints
outcomes: A cloud model API lets you send messages without hosting the weights.

lessons.title: Logs, regions, and data you may use
outcomes: A log can contain the person's words.

lessons.title: A one-page policy
outcomes: The page names the corpus, the tools, the cap, and the approver.

lessons.title: Capstone and certifications
outcomes: Finish a grounded helper on notes you wrote.

lessons.title: Speech in, a model, speech out
outcomes: LiveKit's pipeline page names a cascaded pipeline: speech-to-text, then a language model, then text-to-speech.

lessons.title: Turn-taking and barge-in
outcomes: LiveKit's turns page says turn detection decides when the user has finished speaking and when they start speaking while the agent is talking.

lessons.title: Latency budgets you label
outcomes: LiveKit's pipeline page says voice conversations feel natural when end-to-end response latency stays under one second. That sentence is LiveKit's, not a measurement from this lab.

lessons.title: Telephony and WebRTC
outcomes: The W3C WebRTC Recommendation of 13 March 2025 defines APIs so media can be sent to and received from another browser or device.

lessons.title: LiveKit Agents and Pipecat
outcomes: LiveKit's pipeline page shows an AgentSession that takes speech-to-text, a language model, and text-to-speech.

lessons.title: A hosted voice agent, from the xAI docs
outcomes: The Speech to Speech page says you connect with a WebSocket to wss://api.x.ai/v1/realtime and pass model as a query parameter.
